title: Pickleball 98
summary: 3D pickleball with real rules, lessons, a ball machine, drills, a walk-around park with open play, a World Tour and online singles and doubles.
body: Pickleball 98 is pickleball in 3D, with real rules and real ball physics. Play the computer, learn the game in Practice, go on a World Tour, play a friend on the same keyboard, or play people online.

list: **Play:** the first choice is **vs Computer** or **Online** (two tabs at the top). vs Computer: singles or doubles against Rookie, Club, Pro or Legend players, and **Where** (below); who exactly you play, the scoring, **World Tour** and **2 Players** are under **More options »**. **Start Match** is the button at the bottom.

**Where and when:** tap **Change** next to Where (on the Play screen, in Practice, or the venue button on the title screen). Pick any of the real venues from My Park, the Venue Finder courts you starred or visited, or one of the five made-up arenas: the court behind the list switches to that venue at once so you can see where you'll play. Then pick the **time of day**: **Now** (the real sky and today's weather there), **Morning**, **Midday**, **Golden hour** or **Night** (under the lights; only where the courts really have lights: not at Sinaloa). Matches, Practice and online rooms then play on that venue's real court. A real court (not an arena) has **Directions** under its name: it opens your maps app with directions there.
**Practice:** lessons with a coach, a ball machine and drills (below).
**My Park:** walk round a public park where games are going on, watch from the bleachers, and put your paddle in a rack to play next (below).
**World Tour:** eight matches from the Park Open to the Center Court Masters. Win to unlock new outfits.
**2 Players:** head to head on one keyboard or two gamepads.
**Online** (Play's second tab): Quick Match, rooms with a code, and invites, at any venue and time of day.

**Drill with a friend** (Practice, or Online > Play: **Drill together**): two people drill together instead of playing points: **Dinks**, **Third-shot drops**, **Volleys**, **Serve and return** or a **Free rally**. Between rallies you both walk to the drill's spots, then one of you feeds the ball (you take turns). The top of the screen counts your **streak** of good shots together (into the kitchen for dinks, a drop from the baseline...), your **best** and the rallies. Make a room and share the code, or invite someone online; Quick Match pairs you with someone who picked the same drill.

The title screen has four places to go: **Play** (vs Computer or Online), **My Park**, **Practice** and **Real Games** (your real-life pickleball), plus **My Player** (pick your player, then the Locker Room) and the venue and time you play (tap it to change). The scene behind the title is that venue. Settings, Controls and Rules are in the Options and Help menus. The first time you open the game it offers a 2-minute lesson. The game chat (the speech bubble in the title bar) opens only when you tap it; a new message shows a number on the bubble.

**A real pickleball:** the ball weighs and flies like a USA Pickleball-approved one. Its holes make it slow down a lot in the air, spin bends it only a little, and it bounces 30-34 inches when dropped from 78 inches, like the rulebook test. Outdoor courts use the 40-hole outdoor ball; indoor venues use the lighter, slower 26-hole indoor ball.

**Spin and the bounce:** topspin dips and kicks forward low after the bounce; slice skids through and stays low (a steep slice dink can check up); sidespin jumps sideways. A ball that clips the net cord can roll over or drop back, and a serve that touches the net and lands in the box plays on (there are no lets).

**Your shot comes from the paddle:** pace, aim and timing set the paddle's angle and speed, and physics does the rest. You can't drive a ball down from below the net: hit it hard from there and it carries long. Misses come from the paddle face being a little open or closed, not from dice.

**Speeds like the pros:** dinks around 10-15 mph, drops 20-25, serves 35-47, drives and speed-ups 40-60. Rookies hit softer and miss more; Pros and Legends hit harder and miss less, but nobody moves faster than a real player.

**Game speed (Settings):** **Medium**, the default, is real life: the ball, how fast the players move and react, and the time between points (about 13 seconds from the last shot to the next serve) were measured from PPA Tour broadcasts. Tap to hurry the wait between points. **Slow** runs the game's clock at 80% to give you more time to learn; **Fast** runs it at 120% with a quick wait between points. Online games run at real speed with the quick wait.

**How the computer plays:** deep serves and deep returns, then the returners come to the kitchen line; a third-shot drop or a drive depending on the return; patient cross-court dinks until a ball is up around the hip, then a speed-up at your paddle side; resets when they're caught in the middle; the odd lob. Doubles teams stack (they keep their forehands in the middle), the net player poaches a floater, and Pros and Legends will go round the kitchen for an Erne or around the post.

**How the players move:** measured from PPA Tour footage. At the kitchen line they wait tall on a wide base (feet wider than the shoulders); at the baseline a little lower. A split step lands as the other side hits without stopping them dead, and a computer player starts toward the new ball about 0.3 seconds later. Computer partners shift across the court with the ball as a pair, so they're still moving as the other side hits, the way pros are. A groundstroke from the baseline comes up out of the crouch, meeting a low ball with a bend at the hips. Shuffles keep the feet apart (on Low graphics too). After a third-shot drop the serving team watches it for a moment, then walks in through the transition zone, still moving as the other side plays the ball (the split step is a hop on the way, not a stop), then on to the line. On an overhead they turn sideways, point the other hand at the ball, step back if it's behind them, then jump into the smash and land. The paddle never passes through anyone's body: walking between points it hangs from the hand outside the leg, running it rides tipped up in front, and through strokes, follow-throughs and celebrations the hand turns it (or moves it) clear of the trunk, legs, head and the other arm, which moves out of its way. Balls are met out in front: a serve is dropped beside the front foot and swung outside the back knee; computer players stand off low balls so they meet them in front of the knees; a ball at the chest or hip is played the way pros do it, with the hand out beside the body or the elbow up and out (the "chicken wing"), leaning back or away from it (a computer player also shifts their hips). Partners walking to their spots pass each other instead of bumping. Your own player still only moves when you move it: for a ball at your body your player only leans and turns.
**Watch out for your body:** a ball that hits you (not your paddle) loses you the point, even if it was going out. The computer steps out of the way of balls going long; you have to as well.

**Learn to play like a pro:** ten short lessons in the order a point is played. Coach Pat gives a two- or three-sentence tip with a little moving court picture, then you try it on court and the coach tells you how it went. Done lessons get a check mark.

**Ball Machine:** pick what it feeds (dinks, third-shot feeds, drives, volleys, lobs or a random mix) and how fast. **More options »** has spin, placement (forehand, backhand, middle, random, alternate), balls a minute, how many balls and target zones. Zones on their court light up with points when you land in them. Pause any time; at the end you see in/out/net, accuracy and your average speed.

**Drills:** one goal each, 1-3 minutes, up to three stars: serve targets, return deep and move in, third-shot drops, keeping 10 dinks in a row going, resets from mid-court, hand battles, overhead smashes and split-step timing.
After every shot a one-word label shows what it was (Drop, Dink, Drive, Pop-up, Out, Net...). Make the same mistake twice and a tip says what to change.

body: **My Park** (on the title screen, after Practice) is a public park with four courts, each with a real game of doubles going on between the park's regulars: Court 1 is for Rookies, Courts 2 and 3 for Club players, Court 4 for Pros. The regulars walk between the courts, sit on the benches and bleachers, chat, clap a great point, and put their paddles in the racks to play next. The time of day follows your clock: at night the court lights come on.

list: **Walk** on a phone: put your thumb down anywhere in the lower part of the screen (held sideways: the left side) and slide it; a faint ring shows under your thumb and follows it. A little push walks, more jogs, all the way (held) runs (the knob turns yellow). You turn the way you point at once, and pulling the stick toward you turns you round to come back. Drag anywhere else on the picture, with your other thumb, to look around (up and down too); **double tap** the picture to bring the camera round behind you. The camera only turns when you turn it, so the way you're walking never changes by itself; if you'd rather it came round behind you as you walk: Menu > **Camera: Follow behind** (tap again for **Camera: Free**). On a computer: the arrow keys or W A S D (Shift sprints), drag the picture (or Q and E) to look. Only you move yourself. **Options > Move Pad on the Right** puts the walking side on the right.

**Always in sight:** walk under a deck, a pergola, a tent or a shade roof and it fades away while you're under it (or while it's between the camera and you); a tree the camera is in steps aside for a moment. Watching a court, the camera finds a spot where the whole court shows.

**One button** (top right) shows what you can do where you stand: **Watch** by a court's bleachers, **Call next** at its paddle rack, **Sit** at a bench, **Locker Room** at the pro shop, **Ball Machine** at the practice court.
**Watch:** you sit on the bleachers and the view moves to the court; **Cam** changes the angle (sideline, baseline, high) and **Leave** walks on. Only that court's score shows.

**Call next:** your paddle goes in the rack. When the game on that court ends and it's your turn, you're on court for a game of doubles to 11 with the regulars, with your usual controls. Then it's back to the park. Tap the rack again to take your paddle back.

**Park rep:** every game counts: a win more, a streak and the harder courts more still. Your level (Newcomer, Regular, Local, Court Boss, Park Legend) and record show on your nameplate for other people.
**The menu** (top left) lists the courts with their scores (Watch any of them), has short things to say and cheers (and **Wave**), the Locker Room, and Leave My Park.

body: My Park is also a place to just be. Regulars sit on the benches together chatting, wait their turn by the paddle racks, and wave and say hi to you by name as you pass (the ones who know you remember your last games).

list: **Sit** on any bench or bleacher with the one button. A friend online who's sitting near you shows **Sit with Ali**: you take the seat next to them, and they see you there.

**Hang out** in the park menu: **Chill mode** hides everything on screen for a calm view of the park (tap **☾ Chill** at the bottom to bring it back; the move pad still works, faintly). **Music** plays a soft lo-fi loop made by the game itself (quiet). **Golden hour** puts the sun low and warm (tap again for the real sky now).

body: Online, other players in the same park walk around with you, with their names over them, and can call next on the same court: then you play each other (computer players fill the other spots). A park holds 16 people; more open another one.

body.h: Tennis, hoops, the gym and the TV

body: Some venues have more than pickleball, and in My Park you can use what's really there. Walk up to it and the one button (top right on a phone) says what you can do: **Play tennis** at a tennis court, **Shoot hoops** at a basketball court, **Work out** in a gym, **Watch TV** where a lobby, bar or gym has one. Only places a venue really has: tennis at Los Cab, Newport, Whittier Narrows and the Paseo Club (their tennis courts on the map); basketball at Sinaloa and Bouquet Canyon (their courts on the map) and Los Cab's indoor gym; the gym at Los Cab's fitness centre and the Paseo Club's fitness floor and performance centre; TVs at Los Cab (lobby, fitness centre), the Paseo Club (lobby, fitness floor, bar), SMASH (lobby video wall, bar, by the courts) and Whittier Narrows (under the shade roof). **Leave** (top right) puts you back where you were.

list: **Tennis:** a quick casual game. **vs the computer** is first to 4 games (no-ad: at 40-40 the next point wins; pick Easy, Normal or Hard under More options); **Rally challenge** counts how many you hit back in a row. Run with the move pad; **swipe up** to hit: the angle aims left or right, how far up goes deep or short, a faster swipe hits harder (and is less sure). You can swipe a little early: the racket meets the ball when it arrives. A yellow ring shows where their shot will bounce; swipe up to serve. On a computer: arrow keys or WASD to run, Space to hit (K hard, L a lob).

**Shoot hoops:** walk anywhere on the court and **swipe up** to shoot: how far up is how hard (the meter's green band, about half way up, is just right), the angle aims. Swishes, banks off the glass and rims come off as a real ball would. **Shoot around** keeps makes, streaks and swishes; **Around the World** is seven spots round the key (stand in the yellow ring), make each to move on; **H-O-R-S-E** against the computer: make a shot and they must make it from the same spot or take a letter; miss and it's their turn to set one. On a computer: hold Space for power, let go to shoot.

**Work out:** a workout as a rhythm game. **Today's workout** is five moves (squats, curls, presses, rows, jumping jacks, sprints on a treadmill if the gym has one) for 20 seconds each, the same for everyone today; **Quick set** is one move for 30 seconds (pick it under More options). Tap the screen (swipe down for rows) when each dot reaches the ring: Perfect, Good or Miss; a streak multiplies your points. Your workouts build your **Fitness** (Locker Room > Trophies): after a workout your player is a build stronger for half an hour, and for good once you're Fit (**Show my gains** there turns it off).

**Real workout** (Work out > More options): the phone's front camera counts your real reps instead of taps, with more room on the timing. It uses the same free pose model as Twin Replay, loaded the first time, and runs on this phone: no picture or video leaves it (the model's usage ping to Google is blocked too). Stand back so the camera sees you from head to knees.

**Watch TV:** you sit where a seat faces the set (or stand), and it shows **Live** (a friend's game, live, through Live Broadcast), **My videos** (a video file you pick on this device: your highlight reels too) playing on the TV itself. Never a TV broadcast.

Your results (tennis wins and best rally, hoops makes and streaks, workouts and fitness) are kept on this device with the game's other settings, and show in the Locker Room under **Trophies**. Nothing is added to the venues for any of this: if a venue's court, gym or TV isn't on the map or in our pictures of the place, it isn't offered (Wolf + Bear has none of these).

body.h: Swimming, the hot tub, food and drinks

body: Where a venue really has a pool, a hot tub, a bar, a cafe or a snack window, walk up to it and the one button offers it: **Swim** at a pool's edge, **Hot tub**, **Order** at a counter, **Get a drink** at a drinks machine or fridge. Only what's really there: pools at Los Cab (the 50 m pool and the lap pool) and the Paseo Club; the hot tub by Los Cab's 50 m pool; food and drinks at Los Cab Cafe, Newport's clubhouse bar and social lawn bar, Whittier Narrows' snack window, the Paseo Club's cafe and bar and SMASH's bar and restaurant; drinks machines at Los Cab Cafe, SMASH's lobby and Wolf + Bear's spectator strip.

list: **Swim:** **Swim** gets you in where you stand, **Cannonball!** jumps in off the edge. Push the move pad to swim (freestyle; push it all the way for faster), let go to tread water, **Float** lies you on your back. **Get out** (top right) climbs out at the nearest edge. In a lap pool, **A length** (Los Cab's 50 m pool) or **Laps** (two lengths of the Paseo Club's pool) races the clock from the wall in your lane: at the far wall the view turns round so pushing up the pad swims you home; your best time is kept.

**Hot tub:** you sit back on the bench inside with your arms along the rim; the water bubbles and steams, the view drifts slowly round, and the park's lo-fi music comes on (**♪ Music** turns it off; your music setting comes back when you get out).

**Order** and **Get a drink:** a short menu of original drinks and food (smoothies, lemonade, coffee, a burger, fries, tacos, a wrap; at a machine, cold drinks). Prices are in **Casino 98's play chips**, the same bank as the casino games (no real money; run low and the house tops you up). What you buy is in your player's hand: **Sip** (or **Bite**) a few times until it's gone, or **×** to put it down. Getting in the water or going to play puts it down.
**Somebody by a drinks machine looks awfully hot and thirsty...** (a little secret: it pays to be kind).

Your best swim times and how often you've ordered are kept on this device. Nothing is added to the venues: a pool, a hot tub or a bar that isn't on the map or in our pictures of the place isn't offered (Newport's map shows a pool and spa, but they're in a neighbour's garden, not the club's).

body.h: Living Park: clones and regulars who remember you

list: **Leave your clone in the park:** My Park's menu > **My clone in the park...** > **Leave my clone at** this venue. While you're away, other players at that venue find **your clone** by the entrance and can walk up and **Challenge** it to a game of singles; it plays the way your films say you play. You need your own clone first (Twin Replay > Stats > Make a Clone, with **This is me**). **Take it back** removes it. It's only ever in one venue, and only while you're away.

**What it may say:** your clone never makes up words. It only says the lines in **What it may say** (hello, when it wins, when it loses, a bit of trash talk, encouragement), which you write or keep; the game picks one that fits the moment. Up to 20 lines of 60 characters.

**Playing a friend's clone:** walk up to it and press **Challenge**. The result card shows the line their clone picked. Your friend gets a notification ("Your clone lost to Sam 7-11 at Los Cab"; Do Not Disturb holds it like any other) and, when they come back to My Park, a **While you were away** card with who played it and the scores. Their clone's log keeps the last 50 games.

**The regulars remember you:** at each venue the first few regulars say hello by name and remember the last time you met and your recent results there ("Saw you win 11-7 against Alice's clone"). They also keep a day: quieter in the morning, busiest for evening open play, and they say so. Their memory stays on this device.

body: **My Park** first asks **where to?**: Riverside Park, or one of eight real Southern California venues: Los Cab Sports Village (Fountain Valley), The Tennis & Pickleball Club at Newport Beach, Wolf + Bear Indoor Pickleball (Van Nuys), iPickle Whittier Narrows (South El Monte), The Paseo Club (Valencia), Sinaloa Middle School (Simi Valley), California SMASH (El Segundo) and Bouquet Canyon Park (Santa Clarita: the city's 8 outdoor courts, two rows of four on what were two tennis courts). Tap one to go; **☆** stars your favorites so they're first. **Change venue...** is in the park's menu.

**One place:** the venue you walk in My Park is where you play (Play and Practice pick it up), and the venue you pick for a match is where My Park opens. Your time of day carries too. Play a game on a court in My Park and the next match at that venue is on the same court. Real courts have no umpire's chair, so nobody sits by the net.

The real venues have real surfaces (court grain, asphalt, grass, stucco, tile roofs, wood and tile floors) and sun shadows that follow the time of day. On an older phone, **Options > Graphics: Low** goes back to the simpler flat look and runs faster (it applies the next time you open a venue).

**Photoreal backdrop** (My Park's menu): put a real, photographic 3D copy of the place behind your venue's courts. **Capture this court** films a slow 20-40 second walk around the court, then Meta's free MapAnything service on Hugging Face builds it in 3D (about a minute; it uses your own free daily allowance there and can be busy). Or **Import a splat file** made with a capture app (.ply, .spz, .splat, .ksplat, .sog) (only real captures: there's no made-up demo). Then **Line it up** by tapping the court's four corners in the view from above. Backdrops are kept in C:\My Splats (up to 3; up to 8 MB they sync with your files). Graphics: Low hides them.

**Real Sky** (on Medium and High): every venue shows the real sky for where it is, right now. The sun and the moon sit where they really are for that court's location and the time, so shadows fall the way they do there today, and sunsets, twilight and stars follow the real clock. The day's weather comes from Open-Meteo for that venue: clouds, rain or snow (the court gets wet), wind in the trees, and haze or fog. Indoors you see the weather only through the doors and windows. **Options > Sky** turns it off, or picks a fixed sky for fun: Clear, Cloudy, Rain, Sunset or Night. **Real Weather at Classic Venues** (off by default) gives the classic courts a real place's weather today too, keeping their own time of day. Only the venue's location is used, never yours.

list: Each venue is built from the real map: every court where it really is and turned the way it's turned, its banks of fences, the clubhouse and other buildings round it, parking lots, trees and palms, and for the indoor clubs the hall itself (walls, a door, the lights, and at SMASH the raised lounge and the bar). Court colors and the look come from what the clubs look like; the drawing is 98ish's own.

A few courts at each venue have live games, regulars and a paddle rack (they're numbered like the venue's own courts, e.g. **Court 35**), and the other courts have people playing too. Your game is played **on the court you walked up to**, with the rest of the venue round you.
Online, friends who pick the **same venue** meet there. Different venues are different parks.

**Any court on Earth (Venue Finder).** At the top of **where to?**, type a court's name, a town or a US ZIP code and tap **Find**, or tap **Near me**. It searches every pickleball venue in OpenStreetMap (over 11,000 venues with 34,000 courts worldwide, most of them in the US and Canada, where the map knows pickleball best) right on your device. Tap one and 98ish **builds it from the map** (a few seconds; up to about half a minute the first time anyone visits it): its courts at their real size and angle, fences, lights where the map says so, buildings, parking, paths and trees round it. Indoor venues get a hall from the building's outline. Star ☆ the ones you like. Filters (indoor, lights, 8+ courts, public) are under **Filters**. Friends who pick the same court meet there too.

Venue Finder builds what the map knows, nothing more: a court missing from OpenStreetMap is missing here, and colors fall back to the classic blue court on green when the map doesn't say. You can fix the map itself at openstreetmap.org, and the next monthly update picks it up. Venue data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

**Walk in like you would in real life.** At **Los Cab** you arrive in the parking lot, go through the front doors into the lobby (fountain, front desk, pro shop), down the hall past the locker rooms (each with a sauna and a steam room) and out to the 50 m pool, then on to the courts; the cafe, lounge, fitness centre, spin studio, racquetball, indoor gym, kids club and day spa are all open. At **California SMASH** you walk up the Maple Ave frontage, through the front doors into the lobby, through the bar and restaurant (and past the restrooms) out to the courts and the raised lounge, and out to the patio by the train viaduct. Inside, the camera comes closer and stays in the room. Upstairs spaces (SMASH's VIP mezzanine, Los Cab's ballroom) are shown but not walkable yet.

**What's around each venue is real, too.** The buildings, golf course, parks and big roads past the venue's edge come from OpenStreetMap (at their mapped heights), and the skyline is the real one from free elevation data: the San Gabriel Mountains north of Whittier Narrows, the hills round Valencia and Simi Valley, the ocean and Catalina from Newport. Nothing is made up to fill the view: where the map doesn't know, nothing is drawn.
Some details are best guesses (for example where Wolf + Bear's private court is, or which tennis courts at Whittier Narrows have pickleball lines). No location is needed or used.
Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License. Skyline: AWS Terrain Tiles (USGS 3DEP, SRTM).

body.h: Twin Replay: your real games, replayed

body: **Game > Twin Replay** turns a video of a real game into a replay in Pickleball 98: the players move where you all really moved and swing when you really hit, at your court (pick one of the real venues and the court number), with stats for everyone.

list: **Film a game** (in Pickleball 98, with the back camera) or **Open a video** you filmed. Best: the phone on the back fence behind a baseline, sideways, the whole court in the picture, sound on (the paddle's pop times the hits).

**Tap the four corners** of the court in the order shown (hold and slide for a magnifier, drag a dot to fix it). Yellow lines show the court as the game now sees it. Pick **Doubles** or **Singles**, then **Read the game**.

Reading happens on this device: a pose model (Google's MediaPipe, free) finds the players in each picture, about 15 pictures for each second of video. It takes a while (a progress bar shows the time left; Pause and Stop work). Then name the players by their shirt color.

**Replay:** each rally plays on the athletes. Play/pause, the rally's timeline (ticks are the hits), speed (1x, ½x, ¼x), **Camera** (Broadcast, Side, Top, Follow one player, Fence: where your phone was). **More options »** shows your video beside it in sync, changes the venue and court, and sends the game to a friend.

**Stats:** rally lengths and highlights (tap one to watch it), and for each player where they stood (a heat map of their half), time at the kitchen line, meters covered, their shot mix (serve, return, drive, drop, dink, volley, overhead, lob), third-shot choices, and how often they hit a rally's last shot.

**Send to a friend** makes a small replay file (no video: just everyone's positions and the hits); they open it in **Twin Replay > More options » > Open a replay file...**. **Try the demo rally** (under More options) shows what it does without filming anything.
Honest limits: the shot kinds are a good guess, not a referee. People walking through, or a player hidden behind another, can confuse it for a moment.

body.h: Real Ball: line calls and the real ball's flight

body: While Twin Replay reads a video it also looks for **the ball** in every picture (a small yellow thing that moves between pictures), then fits each shot's flight with the game's own ball physics (gravity, a holed ball's drag, the bounce), from the hit to the next player's paddle. Where it's sure, the replay shows the **real** flight instead of a rebuilt one.

list: **Challenge** (on the replay bar, when a rally has measured bounces): the camera swoops down to where the ball landed, a green or red mark shows the spot, and it says **IN by 3 cm**, **OUT by 4 cm**, or **Too close: call stands** when the margin is within the measurement's uncertainty. **Another call** steps through the rally's other bounces.
Lines are in (a ball touching any part of a line is in), except on a serve, where the kitchen line belongs to the kitchen (touching it is a fault); the centerline counts for both service courts.

**Stats** gets a **Real Ball** card: each player's fastest and typical shot speed (km/h), the line calls, and a map of every bounce. Coach uses the measured landing of your third shots ("Drop landed 0.6 m inside their kitchen").

Best results: film at 30 or 60 frames a second from the back fence, steady, the whole court in view, good light. A blurry or tiny ball, or a shot the camera barely saw, falls back to the rebuilt flight (and gets no line call).
It's a careful measurement, not an official one: the uncertainty is shown, and close calls stand. Everything runs on this device; nothing is uploaded.

body.h: Highlights: a highlight film of your game

body: In a Twin Replay game, the **Highlights** tab picks the best rallies (the longest, the fastest shots, close line calls, kitchen battles, the biggest runs) and cuts a broadcast-style film of them: your own video of each point, a **3D replay** of the best one from the TV angle, the **Hawk-Eye** view of close calls in slow motion, a score bug and shot speeds on screen, a title and an end card with the game's stats, and a soundtrack made for it.

list: Reorder or remove moments with the arrows and the ✕, then **Make the film**. Keep Pickleball 98 open while it's made: the 3D parts are filmed as they play (about as long as the film).
**Save to Device** puts the video (MP4, about 60 seconds at 720p) in your phone's Files or Photos; **Share...** sends it to any app.
Everything is made on this device: the film never goes to a server unless you share it. The music is generated, so it's yours to post. Games kept without their video get a film of 3D replays.

body: A **clone** is a computer player that plays like a real person, learned from their Twin Replay games: where they stand (do they rush the kitchen line or stay back?), how fast they move and react, their third shot (drop or drive), what they do at the kitchen line (dink or speed it up), resets, lobs, where their dinks and drives go, how deep their serve is.

list: Open a game in Twin Replay, go to **Stats** and press **Make a Clone of...** under a player. Tick **This is me** for yourself. Make more clones from more games, or pick **Add to** an existing clone: the meter goes from "A first guess" to "Plays just like them". With little film a clone plays close to the level it starts from (Rookie, Club, Pro, Legend) and moves toward the real person as it sees more.

**Play** a clone: on the **Play** screen pick it under **Against** (or as your **Partner** in doubles; clones are at the top as "Clone: name"), or in **Twin Replay > More options » > Your clones**. **Rematch against the clones** (a game's More options) puts you back in that game's matchup at the same venue and court, everyone else played by their clone.

**Sharing:** only your own clone (made with This is me) can be sent: **Share...** in Your clones makes a small file (a few KB: counts of what you did, no video); your friend opens it with **Open a friend's clone...**. A clone you made from your video of someone else is labeled "Built from your video" and stays on this device; to play their clone together, they make and share their own.

Honest limits: a clone copies tendencies the video can show (positions, shot kinds, timing); it can't copy touch or spin exactly, and the video can't tell a winner from an error, so how often their shots end rallies only nudges the clone's accuracy.

body.h: Go Live: friends watch your real game in 3D

body: **Real Games > Go Live** (or Game > Go Live...) streams a real game as you play it: other players watch it live in Pickleball 98, the athletes moving where you all move, at your venue and court.

list: Pick the venue and court and type the players' names (near side = by the phone). **Point the camera**: put the phone on the back fence, on its side, the whole court in the picture; tap the four corners like in Twin Replay, then **Go live**. Other players see you're live in Real Games; **Share the link** sends it to anyone else.

While live, the phone reads the players and listens for the paddle; the little court in the corner shows who it's following. Tap **Point: near / Point: far** after each rally to keep the score (side-out, with the full call) for everyone watching.

**Watching**: tap the notice (or Real Games > a player "is live", or the LIVE strip in My Park at that venue). The game plays about a second behind real time, with Broadcast, Side, Top and Follow cameras, the score, reactions, how many are watching, and **⟲ 10 s** to see the last moment again (**Go live** catches up). In **My Park** at the same venue the real players are on that court as you walk by.
**End broadcast** stops it; the game is kept in your **Twin Replay** games (positions and hits, no video), and viewers can keep a copy too.

Only where everyone is, the hits and the score leave the phone: never the picture or the sound. A slower phone streams a little less smoothly (the players are carried along between readings); a phone's graphics chip reads several pictures a second.

body.h: Coach: what your film says about your game

body: **Coach** (Real Games > **Coach**, or a Twin Replay game's **Stats > Coach ... on this game**) reads your part of your filmed games and compares 13 habits with what Rookie, Club, Pro and Legend players do: getting to the kitchen line after the return (or your team's third shot), a split step right as they hit, paddle up at the line, getting back to your spot, speed around the court, third shots that work, dinks kept in play, speeding up only high balls, resets from mid-court, serve and return depth, how often your shot ends the point, and spacing with your partner.

list: **Your game**: each habit with your number, the target level's number and a verdict (On target, Close, Work on it, Need more film), plus a level estimate with an honest range. Tap a habit for what it means and **Watch** buttons: the replay jumps to a real moment from your film, slowed down, with a **see-through player doing it the Pro way** beside you (for movement habits).

**Plan**: **Make my plan** picks your three biggest fixable weaknesses and builds three short practice sessions from Pickleball 98's drills (sized to how big the gap is), with three cues to remember. **Start** opens the drill. The cues also show on your Real Games sessions.
**Progress**: each game you're in adds a point to a small chart per habit, with the target line; it says better, worse or steady. Coach also counts the weeks in a row you filmed or practiced.
Pick yourself in each game (Coach asks; More options lists them) and your target level (More options). More games make it surer: each habit says how many times it was seen.

Honest limits: it's only as good as Twin Replay's reading of the video; the ball isn't tracked (shot kinds come from where people stood and moved), and a winner and an error look the same. "Paddle up" needs games read after this update.

steps: **Serve deep** (and return deep): it keeps the other side back at their baseline.
**Let it bounce twice:** the serve and the return must bounce before anyone volleys.
**Returning? Come in.** After a deep return, go straight to the kitchen line.
**Serving? Drop the third shot** softly into their kitchen, then move up together.
**Live at the kitchen line,** but never volley in the kitchen or let your momentum carry you in after a volley.
**Dink patiently,** low and cross-court, until a ball comes up above the net. Then **speed it up** at their hip or shoulder.
**In trouble mid-court? Reset:** a soft tap into their kitchen, then step in.
**In doubles, move as a unit** with your partner; a ball down the middle goes to the player with the forehand there.

body: Aim at their court, then press and hold **hit**, and let go just before the ball reaches you (the marker on the meter in the green). How long you held it decides the pace:

list: A quick **tap** is soft: a dink at the kitchen line, or a drop or reset from farther back.
A long **hold** is hard: a drive, a speed-up or a counter.
A soft ball aimed deep goes up high: a lob.

body: The little ring on the ball turns orange when you'll meet it above the net: that one you can attack. Below the net, keep it soft. To **serve**, hold hit to fill the serve meter and let go in the green.

With the mouse or keys (and Classic touch), a small dot on their court shows where your shot will go, colored by the pace you're holding (blue soft, yellow firm, orange hard). There's no line showing the ball's path: you read the ball, not a guide. Your paddle leaves a short trail through each swing (Settings > Swing trail turns it off).

Let go just as the ball gets to you. A **perfect** contact (the word shows in gold) is cleaner and a little faster; the game freezes for a split second and the camera punches in. Three, five and eight perfect in a row get a shout, and so do runs of points and comebacks. Let go too early and the swing waits up to a second for the ball; if the ball has already gone past you, it's called a miss right away (never after the point is over). A ball passing just beyond your arm still gets a stretch, but a long reach is less accurate. When everyone is at the kitchen line the camera closes in a little.
On phones that can vibrate, your hits and points give a short buzz; an iPhone can't, so the edges of the screen glow instead. Options > **Hit Buzz** turns both off.

On a touch screen, the swipe you just made is drawn on the screen as you make it: a smooth stroke that follows your finger, thin where you started and full at your fingertip. It takes the color of the shot (blue soft, yellow firm, orange hard, purple a lob, gray a miss) and fades away about half a second after you lift. With Classic controls you get a small ripple where you touch instead, and a bigger one, in the pace's color, where you let go. Turn it off in Settings > Show swipe trail (or Options > Show Swipe Trail).

The ball sounds like real pickleball: the bright "pock" of the paddle face ringing at about 1,200 Hz for a few hundredths of a second, softer on a dink, sharper on a drive or a put-away, duller off the edge of the paddle. Each paddle design rings a little differently. Bounces are a lower, duller "tock", the net a soft thud and rattle, and the fence a metallic clatter. Shots far away are quieter and a little duller. The volume follows the taskbar's speaker.

During a match the screen keeps just the score, Pause, one hint line for your first few points, and the controls. What the umpire and the crowd say comes up one line at a time in the middle and goes away by itself. The camera (Broadcast, TV high, Sideline, Behind you) is in the pause menu (or press C); Broadcast, high behind you, is the clearest. TV cuts to the server between points are optional (Settings).

keys: W A S D or the arrows

body.phone: You always move your player yourself: drag on the move pad (bottom left, or bottom right: Pause > Settings > Move pad). Nothing moves your player for you. The first time you play you pick how you hit, and you can switch any time in Pause > Settings > Touch controls. **Swipe:** put a finger down anywhere off the pad and swipe up toward where the ball should go, letting go as the ball comes: the direction is where across their court, the length how deep, the speed the pace (a quick flick is hard, a slow swipe soft, a slow long swipe a lob); a tap is a soft touch shot (a dink). To serve, swipe the same way. **Classic:** touch their court to aim (elsewhere, drag to steer), hold for pace and let go as the ball comes.
body.computer: Move with the keys, aim with the mouse, and click (or press Space) to hit. Two players on one keyboard: Player 1 uses W A S D and F, Player 2 the arrows and L; while holding hit, your move keys steer the aim. A gamepad works too. Change any key in **Controls**.

body: Open **My Player** on the title screen and pick **Locker Room...** (or Game > Locker Room...) to dress any player. Drag the player to turn them around, and pick **Jogging** to see the kit move.

list: **Body:** the **face** (photographed faces, each with its own skin tone and hair color, or Classic for the modeled one), skin, hair and hair color (a photographed face's own short hair takes the color you pick; **Shaved** shaves it), a beard, height and build; **Plays** (right- or left-handed) and **Pro style** (a compact all-court game with a one-handed backhand, or an aggressive two-hander with a two-handed backhand).
**Kit:** a theme (Classic whites, Club colors, Pro kit, Beach, Winter, Retro 80s/90s, Casual) and its style, your two kit colors, then any top, bottom and socks.
**Gear:** hats (caps, visor, headband, bucket hat, beanie), sunglasses, wristbands, gloves and shoes.
**Paddle:** a design and its colors.

body: Your look is saved with your user profile and goes with you online, so other people see it. **Auto by venue** puts everyone in the venue's kit (beach kit at Sandy Point, winter kit at Frost Hollow); **Computer players: Random kits** dresses the computer's players in kits of their own.

body.tip: Settings > Graphics: Medium and High show the full players with their photographed faces and clothes (High: sharper skin and faces); **Ultra** (for a strong computer) adds soft shadows where bodies meet (ambient occlusion), the venue's sky in the players' light and a soft glow; Low draws them simply (colors and the main pieces) for slow phones.

title: Pickleball 98: Real Games
summary: Score your real pickleball games, plan open play with your group, and keep a friendly ladder.
body: **Real Games** is the part of Pickleball 98 for the pickleball you play in real life. Pick **Real Games** on the title screen (or Game > Real Games...). It has five tabs:

list: **Play**: your group's sessions and your courts. **New Session...** picks the court, day, time and how many players, and invites other players by their player names; each person answers **I'm in**, **Maybe** or **Can't**. When it's full, more "in"s go on a **waitlist** and the first one is told as soon as a spot opens. On the day: **Running late?** (5 to 30 minutes, or **I'm here**), a little chat, and the **courts**: everyone who's in gets a court each round, sit-outs rotate fairly. Choose **Mix it up** (new partners every round), **King of the court** (tap the winners: they move up a court and split up) or **Two groups** (one from each group on every team, for mixed doubles). **Score this game** opens the scorekeeper with those players.
**Tournaments**: weekly in-game tournaments at the real venues (below).

**Score**: the courtside scorekeeper. Pick the players (you, other players by name, or a guest) and **Start Game**, then tap whichever team won each rally. It shows the score call ("4-2-1": serving team, receiving team, server 1 or 2), who serves from which side and who receives, says **Side out**, **Switch ends** at 6 (8 in a game to 15, 11 to 21) and **Game point**, and can say the score out loud. **Undo** takes back the last rally. The screen stays on during a game, and a game in progress survives a reload or a locked phone.

**Matches**: every match you've played. A match counts once **someone on the other team confirms** it (they get a notification); **That's Wrong** sends it back. Nobody confirms in 7 days: it expires. To take back a confirmed match, **Remove...** asks the other team to agree. **Log a Match...** adds one you scored on paper.
**Ladder**: the friends' ratings (doubles and singles) for everyone you've played or planned with, and your record, streaks, last 10, best partners and head-to-head.

body: Every week there are in-game tournaments at the real venues, with made-up names (they aren't real events and aren't connected with the venues or any real tournament): the **Fountain Valley Fall Classic** at Los Cab (Saturdays 10 AM), the **Narrows Open** at Whittier Narrows (Sundays 2 PM), the **Back Bay Invitational** at Newport (Fridays 6 PM), the **Van Nuys Night Slam** at Wolf + Bear (Thursdays 7:30 PM), the **Valencia Twilight Cup** at Paseo (Wednesdays 6 PM), the **Beach Cities Indoor Open** at SMASH (Tuesdays 7 PM), the **Simi Schoolyard Shootout** at Sinaloa (Saturdays 4 PM), the **Canyon Country Classic** at Bouquet Canyon (Sundays 10 AM) and the **Riverside Nightly** (every day at 8 PM). Times are California time.

steps: Pick a player name, open **Real Games > Tournaments** (or tap the 🏆 chip in My Park at that venue) and tap a tournament.

Pick a division (Doubles 3.0-3.5, Doubles 4.0+, Mixed or Singles) and, for doubles, a partner: another player by name (they tap **Accept** in their Tournaments tab) or a computer partner. Tap **Sign up**.
At the start time the bracket is drawn: computer teams fill it to 4, 8 or 16. Each round has **30 minutes**.

Your match shows at the top with **Play now**: against computer players it starts right there at the venue; against people, **Make a room for this match** (they see **Join the room**) and play online. The result goes in by itself when the game ends (**Report a score** is under More options if it didn't).
body.title: To play in a tournament:

body: If a round's time runs out: against computer players they go through; between people, a team that tapped **We're here** (or made the room) goes through, otherwise it's drawn by lots. The winners and runners-up get a trophy on the **Trophies** tab of the Locker Room. During your match the score shows like a TV broadcast: the tournament, the two teams and the round.

body.h: Scoring options (More options on the Score tab)

body: Singles or doubles; **side-out** scoring (only the serving team scores; in doubles both partners serve, except the very first turn of the game: "0-0-2") or **rally** scoring (every rally scores; with **Win only on your serve**, a team can only win the game on its own serve); play to 11, 15 or 21; win by 2 or 1; one game or best of 3 or 5; who serves first.

Everyone starts at 1500. Each confirmed game moves the winners up and the losers down: more for beating someone rated higher, a bit more for a blowout than an 11-10. In doubles your own rating counts most, so the stronger partner is expected to win more (gains less, loses more). New players move faster for their first 10 games. **Level** is a rough guide (1500 is about 3.5), not an official rating. Games with a guest are in your record but not the ratings. Change the season (all time, this year, the last 90 or 30 days) above the ladder.
In a session, **I'm here** (next to Running late?) tells everyone in it you've arrived.

The Play tab lists Los Cab Sports Village, The Tennis & Pickleball Club at Newport Beach, Wolf + Bear Indoor Pickleball, iPickle Whittier Narrows, The Paseo Club, Sinaloa Middle School, California SMASH and Bouquet Canyon Park, with **Directions** (opens your maps app with directions there) and **Plan** (a session there). Outdoor sessions in the next week show the weather.

body.phone: Keep Pickleball 98 open on the court: iPhone web apps can't keep a screen awake or talk once they're in the background. The spoken score uses your phone's own voice, so nothing is sent anywhere.

body.note: Tournament sign-ups show your player name to everyone who looks at that tournament, and the bracket keeps it for 14 days. Sessions, RSVPs, chat and matches are kept on the Pickleball 98 server for your group.

title: Playing games online
summary: Quick Match, private rooms with a code, join links and computer players.
body: Most games for two or more people have a **Play Online** button with a little globe on it. It also shows how many people are online right now. Your friends can be anywhere: on a phone, a laptop, or across the world.

list: **Quick Match** puts you with the next person who's looking for a game. You're matched with people who picked the same settings.
**Create Room** makes a private room with a short code (like K7QX). Share the code, or use **Copy Link** to send a link that opens the game straight to your room.
**Join with Code** is for when a friend sends you a code. Type it in and you're in their room.
**Invite Someone** lists who's online right now. They get an invitation on their screen.
**Play the Computer** starts right away: computer players fill every other seat.

body.phone: On a phone, Create Room, Join with Code and Invite Someone are under **Play with friends »**, below Quick Match. Once you open it, it stays open in every game.
body.computer: On a computer, Play with friends is open to begin with; **Hide** tucks those three away.

steps: Open the game and choose **Play Online**.
Choose **Create Room** (under **Play with friends** on a phone), and pick the settings you want.
Tap **Copy Code** or **Copy Link** and send it to your friend (in a text, or any chat app).
Your friend opens the same game, chooses **Play Online**, then **Join with Code**.
When everyone is in the room, everyone taps **I'm Ready**, and the host starts the game.
body.title: To play with a friend:

body: The person who made the room is the **host**. The host picks the settings and starts the game. Empty seats can be filled with computer players (**Add Computer Players**), and if someone drops out in the middle of a game, a computer player takes over their seat. If your connection drops, your seat is kept for 30 seconds so you can come back.
When a game ends you can **Rematch**, go **Back to Lobby** to change the settings, or **Leave**. Closing the game window also leaves the room.
Other players see your player name. Playing offline (no name), you can play the computer but not online.

body.tip: The game server takes a nap when nobody is around. If you see "Waking up the game server...", give it up to a minute.
